# Design Decisions
# Key architectural choices made in the docs and their rationale.

decisions:
  - id: DD-001
    title: "File-backed storage instead of database"
    choice: "All data stored as JSON files in .agentrack/ directory"
    rationale:
      - "Zero infrastructure — no database to install, run, or maintain"
      - "Git-native — entire tracker state is version-controlled alongside code"
      - "Conflict-resistant — separate files per issue, separate dependency index"
      - "Agent-friendly — agents can read/write files directly if needed"
      - "Portable — works in any directory, any repo, any machine"
    tradeoffs:
      - "No concurrent write safety beyond file-level (acceptable for agent usage)"
      - "Scalability limited by file count (acceptable — agent trackers are small)"
    status: decided

  - id: DD-002
    title: "Event sourcing for issue state"
    choice: "Issues are append-only event logs; state computed by replay"
    rationale:
      - "Full audit trail — every change is recorded and traceable"
      - "No data loss — updates never overwrite, only append"
      - "Git-friendly — append-only means fewer merge conflicts"
      - "Debuggable — agents can inspect history to understand how an issue evolved"
    tradeoffs:
      - "Read performance requires replaying events (mitigated by index for listing)"
      - "Event files grow over time (acceptable for agent-scale usage)"
    status: decided

  - id: DD-003
    title: "Sorted index with binary search"
    choice: "Index arrays sorted by issue ID (which is time-sortable)"
    rationale:
      - "O(log n) lookup by ID without reading issue files"
      - "ID encodes creation time, so sort is natural and free"
      - "Efficient listing and filtering from index alone"
    tradeoffs:
      - "Insertion requires finding correct position (O(log n) with binary search)"
      - "Index must be kept in sync with issue files"
    status: decided

  - id: DD-004
    title: "Issue ID format: timestamp + random"
    choice: "Date.now().toString(36).slice(0,6) + Math.random().toString(36).slice(-4)"
    rationale:
      - "10 characters — short enough to use in CLI arguments"
      - "Time-sortable — natural ordering reflects creation order"
      - "Collision-resistant — 36^4 randomness per millisecond slot"
      - "Human-readable — easier to work with than UUIDs"
    tradeoffs:
      - "Not globally unique like UUID (acceptable for per-repo scope)"
      - "Timestamp portion leaks creation timing (not a concern here)"
    status: decided

  - id: DD-005
    title: "Separate dependency index file"
    choice: "Blockages in dependencies.json, not in index.json"
    rationale:
      - "Reduces git conflict surface — agents modifying blockages don't conflict with those modifying issue metadata"
      - "Dependency data has different access patterns (bidirectional lookups)"
      - "Keeps index.json focused on issue metadata"
    status: decided

  - id: DD-006
    title: "Directory-walking resolution for .agentrack/"
    choice: "Walk up from cwd to find .agentrack/ folder"
    rationale:
      - "Monorepo support — different subdirectories can have independent trackers"
      - "Familiar pattern (like .git, .eslintrc, tsconfig.json resolution)"
      - "No configuration needed — just run commands from anywhere in the repo"
    status: decided

  - id: DD-007
    title: "Lightweight token auth (not cryptographic)"
    choice: "Simple tk_ prefixed tokens stored in users.json"
    rationale:
      - "Practical attribution, not security — goal is knowing who did what"
      - "Zero setup — no OAuth, no JWT, no external service"
      - "Agent-friendly — set env var once per session"
      - "Configurable strictness — open/read-only/strict modes fit different needs"
    tradeoffs:
      - "Not secure against intentional impersonation (by design — not the goal)"
      - "Tokens stored in plaintext in users.json (acceptable for non-sensitive use)"
    status: decided

  - id: DD-008
    title: "Hierarchy status constraint propagation"
    choice: "Upward auto-promotion + downward cascade with hard blocks"
    rationale:
      - "Keeps subtree lifecycle coherent — can't mark parent done with open children"
      - "Auto-promotion reduces manual bookkeeping — child starting work promotes parent"
      - "Downward cascade on close is intuitive — closing an epic closes its done stories"
      - "Hard blocks prevent inconsistent states"
    tradeoffs:
      - "Status changes can cascade across multiple files (performance consideration)"
      - "Complexity in implementation — need to walk tree in both directions"
    status: decided

  - id: DD-009
    title: "TypeScript with Bun runtime"
    choice: "TypeScript source, Bun for runtime and tooling"
    rationale:
      - "TypeScript for type safety and good DX in library code"
      - "Bun for fast execution, native TypeScript support, built-in test runner"
      - "npm distribution makes it accessible to any Node/Bun project"
    status: decided

  - id: DD-010
    title: "CLI as primary interface with JSON output"
    choice: "All output as JSON to stdout, errors as JSON to stderr"
    rationale:
      - "Machine-parseable — agents and scripts can consume output directly"
      - "No formatting ambiguity — structured data is unambiguous"
      - "Composable — pipe into jq, other tools, or agent parsers"
      - "stderr/stdout split allows filtering output from errors"
    status: decided

  - id: DD-011
    title: "Monorepo with library and UI packages"
    choice: "Bun workspaces monorepo with packages/library and packages/ui"
    rationale:
      - "Shared development workflow — single repo, single set of tooling"
      - "UI can import library directly as a workspace dependency"
      - "Library is independent — can be published and used without UI"
      - "Bun workspaces are simple and require minimal config"
    tradeoffs:
      - "Slightly more complex CI/CD (two packages to build/test)"
      - "Need to be disciplined about not coupling UI into library"
    status: decided

  - id: DD-012
    title: "Tracker class as single programmatic API entry point"
    choice: "All business logic in a Tracker class; CLI is a thin wrapper calling Tracker methods"
    rationale:
      - "CLI and API are interchangeable — same JSON objects returned"
      - "UI can import Tracker directly without shelling out to CLI"
      - "Single implementation to test — CLI tests only verify arg parsing and output"
      - "Clear separation of concerns — Tracker owns logic, CLI owns I/O"
    tradeoffs:
      - "Tracker class may become large (mitigated by delegating to core modules)"
    status: decided

  - id: DD-013
    title: "Commander for CLI argument parsing"
    choice: "Use commander package for argument parsing"
    rationale:
      - "Battle-tested, well-typed, lightweight"
      - "Handles subcommands, flags, variadic args naturally"
      - "Only runtime dependency besides Bun/Node built-ins"
    tradeoffs:
      - "Adds one dependency (acceptable — widely used, stable)"
    status: decided

  - id: DD-014
    title: "Prettier + ESLint for formatting and linting"
    choice: "Use Prettier for formatting and ESLint with TypeScript plugin for linting, replacing Biome"
    rationale:
      - "Biome caused recurring friction — conflicts with strict TypeScript flags (noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature vs UseLiteralKeys), cognitive complexity false positives, and configuration overhead"
      - "Prettier is the industry standard for formatting — zero config, opinionated, no debates"
      - "ESLint with typescript-eslint has first-class TypeScript support — understands types, no false positives from strict TS flags"
      - "Faster development cycle — fewer tool conflicts means less time debugging linter config"
    tradeoffs:
      - "Two tools instead of one (acceptable — both are well-established and complementary)"
      - "ESLint is slightly slower than Biome (acceptable — still fast enough for this codebase size)"
    status: decided
    decided_date: "2026-05-10"
    replaces: "DD-014 originally chose Biome, replaced after recurring friction during Phase 3"

  - id: DD-015
    title: "tsup for npm build pipeline"
    choice: "Use tsup to compile TypeScript source to distributable npm package (ESM + CJS + .d.ts + CLI binary)"
    rationale:
      - "Purpose-built for TypeScript library builds — single tool for library output + CLI binary"
      - "Generates dual ESM/CJS automatically — works for both Node.js and Bun consumers"
      - "Built-in .d.ts generation — type declarations shipped without extra config"
      - "CLI binary bundled as standalone (includes commander) — zero-dep executable"
      - "Preserves per-file structure for library output — enables tree-shaking by consumers"
      - "Built on esbuild — very fast, Bun-friendly toolchain"
      - "Replaces shipping raw TypeScript source which only worked for Bun consumers"
    tradeoffs:
      - "Adds a build step (acceptable — standard for npm packages)"
      - "Need to verify Node.js compatibility in source (replace Bun.file/Bun.write with node:fs)"
      - "CLI shebang changes from #!/usr/bin/env bun to #!/usr/bin/env node"
    alternatives_considered:
      - "tsc alone — no CJS output, no bundling for CLI, more manual config"
      - "bun build — bundles to single file (bad for library tree-shaking), no .d.ts"
      - "Ship raw TS — only works for Bun consumers, excludes most npm users"
    status: decided
    decided_date: "2026-05-11"

  - id: DD-016
    title: "Hand-written user-friendly documentation (supersedes TypeDoc)"
    choice: "Replace TypeDoc auto-generated API docs with hand-written markdown documentation in docs/markdown/. Future Docusaurus site to serve the markdown files."
    rationale:
      - "TypeDoc exposes internal implementation details that aren't useful to users"
      - "No user onboarding — no getting started guide, no conceptual explanations"
      - "Wrong audience — TypeDoc serves library developers, not users"
      - "Hand-written docs allow curated examples, clear explanations, and user-focused structure"
      - "Markdown files can be served by Docusaurus (or similar) for a proper docs site"
    tradeoffs:
      - "Manual effort to keep docs in sync with API changes (acceptable — API is stable)"
      - "No auto-generation from source (acceptable — public API surface is small)"
    alternatives_considered:
      - "TypeDoc HTML only — internals exposed, no guides, not user-friendly"
      - "TypeDoc with custom filters — complex config, still no guides"
      - "VitePress — good for guides but no auto-gen; markdown files work with both VitePress and Docusaurus"
    spec: .agentic/specs/user-docs-spec.md
    issue: mpdpt4rego
    status: in-progress
    decided_date: "2026-05-20"
    supersedes: "DD-016 originally chose TypeDoc HTML (decided 2026-05-11). Replaced because auto-generated docs don't serve the user audience."

  - id: DD-017
    title: "Dogfooding: agentrack tracks its own development"
    choice: "Use agentrack as the issue tracker for developing agentrack itself"
    rationale:
      - "Real-world validation — every feature is tested by actual usage, not just unit tests"
      - "Dogfooding surfaces UX issues early — if the tool is annoying to use, we feel it immediately"
      - "Living documentation — the .agentrack/ directory in the repo serves as a real example"
      - "No external dependency — we don't need GitHub Issues or Jira to track our own work"
    implementation:
      - "CLI linked globally via `npm link` from packages/library/ — agt command resolves to local build"
      - "Issues stored in .agentrack/ at repo root (not inside packages/library/)"
      - "Workflow: make code changes → `bun run build` in packages/library/ → `agt` picks up fresh build"
    tradeoffs:
      - "Bootstrap paradox — need a working version to track work on making it work (mitigated: Phase 7 is already complete)"
      - "Build step required between code changes and CLI usage (acceptable — fast build with tsup)"
    status: decided
    decided_date: "2026-05-12"

  - id: DD-018
    title: "Independent git branch for issue storage"
    choice: "Store .agentrack/ data on a dedicated orphan branch (_agentrack) mounted as a git worktree"
    rationale:
      - "Branch-independent issues — everyone sees the same issues regardless of code branch (main, feature-x, etc.)"
      - "No merge conflicts — issue data is completely separate from code commits"
      - "Git-native — leverages git worktrees, a well-established mechanism for co-located branches"
      - "Explicit sync model — agt push/pull gives users control over when issue state is shared"
      - "Transparent to existing code — worktree appears as a regular directory, no changes to Tracker/file-io layer"
    implementation:
      - "Orphan branch created via git plumbing (hash-object, mktree, commit-tree) — no branch switching, no working tree mutation"
      - "Worktree mounted at .agentrack/ — appears as regular directory"
      - "Three commands: agt init (worktree setup + data init), agt push (auto-commit + sync), agt pull (sync from remote)"
      - ".agentrack/ added to .gitignore on code branch"
    tradeoffs:
      - "Requires git worktree support (available since git 2.5, 2015)"
      - "Adds complexity to init flow (mitigated by well-tested worktree module)"
      - "No auto-commit on every write — explicit push/pull model (intentional: reduces noise)"
    alternatives_considered:
      - "Separate repo for issues — too heavy, loses the git-native simplicity"
      - "Shared branch with code — issues mixed with code, merge conflicts"
      - "Submodule — complex lifecycle, detached HEAD issues"
      - "No change (status quo) — issues locked to code branch, conflicts in busy repos"
    spec: .agentic/specs/independent-git-spec.md
    issue: mpcwcufhzk
    status: decided
    decided_date: "2026-05-19"
    current_phase: "Complete. All deviations fixed, validated, documented. Parent mpcwcufhzk closed."

  - id: DD-019
    title: "Configurable branch name via pointer file"
    choice: "Store branch name in .agentrack.json at repo root (pointer file) to solve circular config discovery problem. Branch name also stored in config.json inside worktree."
    rationale:
      - "Solves chicken-and-egg: to find config, you need the directory; the directory comes from the config"
      - "Pointer file at fixed well-known location (.agentrack.json) breaks the cycle"
      - "Enables multiple agentrack instances per repo (each on its own orphan branch)"
      - "Enables test isolation (test suites use dedicated branches)"
    implementation:
      - "--branch <name> flag on agt init with normalization (strip leading _, prepend _ for branch, . for dir)"
      - "Reject slashes in branch names (would create nested directories)"
      - "Pointer file read by all commands (push, pull, etc.) to discover active worktree"
      - "Backward compatible: no pointer file → default _agentrack / .agentrack/"
    tradeoffs:
      - "Extra file at repo root (minimal — single JSON line)"
      - "Pointer file must be kept in sync (mitigated: only written during init)"
    spec: .agentic/specs/configurable-branch-spec.md
    issue: mpfm8bilwf
    status: in-progress
    decided_date: "2026-05-21"
    validation_notes: "First implementation had 2 critical bugs: (1) tracker init creates .agentrack/ before branch flag takes effect (double directory), (2) no BRANCH_CONFLICT detection. Fix issue mpfn4dkotn. Lesson: always rebuild dist/ and test CLI behaviorally."

1	# Architecture Knowledge
2	# The complete technical architecture of agt as designed in the docs.
3	
4	repo_structure:
5	  type: "Bun workspaces monorepo"
6	  layout:
7	    root: "package.json (workspace config)"
8	    packages_library: "packages/library/ — the core library (current focus)"
9	    packages_ui: "packages/ui/ — web UI (future, not in scope)"
10	  specs: ".agentic/specs/ — 5 spec files covering architecture, types, API, CLI, phases"
11	
12	library_package:
13	  entry_points:
14	    programmatic: "src/index.ts — exports Tracker class and all types"
15	    cli: "src/bin.ts — shebang entry, calls cli/runner.ts"
16	  modules:
17	    cli:
18	      runner: "commander-based arg parsing and command dispatch"
19	      output: "JSON formatting to stdout/stderr"
20	      commands: "one file per CLI command (init, push, pull, create, update, list, view, history, comments, blockages, users, mentions)"
21	    core:
22	      tracker: "main Tracker class — all public methods, delegates to core modules"
23	      resolution: ".agentrack/ directory walk-up resolution"
24	      events: "event append + replay engine"
25	      index_manager: "sorted index management (insert, update, binary search, childrenOf)"
26	      dependency_manager: "bidirectional dependency map management"
27	      mentions: "IN PROGRESS — mention extraction, indexing, read/unread tracking (issue mpo1tdrjdm)"
28	      auth: "token resolution, mode enforcement"
29	      worktree: "IN PROGRESS — git worktree operations (init, push, pull, scenario detection) for orphan branch _agentrack"
30	      id: "ID generation (timestamp + random base36)"
31	      errors: "typed AgentrackError class with error codes and exit codes"
32	    types:
33	      issue: "IssueProperties, ComputedIssue, IssueId, IssueStatus"
34	      event: "all 8 event type interfaces"
35	      index_file: "IndexFile, IndexEntry"
36	      dependency: "DependenciesFile, BlockageEntry, BlockageInfo"
37	      mention: "IN PROGRESS — MentionEntry, MentionsFile, MentionResult, MentionViewResult (issue mpo1tdrjdm)"
38	      user: "UsersFile, UserEntry, UserInfo"
39	      config: "ConfigFile"
40	      api: "all request/response types for every Tracker method"
41	  design_principle: "CLI is a thin wrapper over Tracker. Every CLI command calls one Tracker method. Both return identical JSON."
42	
43	storage_model:
44	  type: file-backed JSON (no database)
45	  location: .agentrack/ directory, discovered by walking up from cwd
46	  git_storage: "IN PROGRESS — migrating to orphan branch _agentrack via git worktree (issue mpcwcufhzk). Currently stored directly in repo."
47	  rationale: git-commitable, merge-friendly, zero infrastructure, monorepo-compatible
48	
49	file_layout:
50	  config_json:
51	    path: .agentrack/config.json
52	    contents: auth mode (open/read-only/strict), defaultUser setting
53	    created_by: init command
54	    mutable: true (manual edit)
55	
56	  index_json:
57	    path: .agentrack/index.json
58	    structure:
59	      open: "sorted array of issue summaries (by id, which is time-sortable)"
60	      closed: "sorted array of issue summaries (by id)"
61	      childrenOf: "map of parentId -> childId[] for O(1) child lookups"
62	    index_entry_fields:
63	      - id (10-char: 6 from timestamp base36 + 4 random base36)
64	      - title
65	      - path (relative path to issue file)
66	      - status (idea/todo/in-progress/done/closed)
67	      - assignee
68	      - parentId (nullable)
69	      - tags (string array)
70	      - priority (1-5, default 3)
71	    sorted: true — enables binary search O(log n) by id
72	    maintained_by: create, update, delete commands
73	
74	  issues_directory:
75	    path: .agentrack/issues/
76	    pattern: one JSON file per issue named [issue_id].json
77	    contents: append-only array of events
78	
79	  dependencies_json:
80	    path: .agentrack/dependencies.json
81	    structure:
82	      blockedBy: "map of issueId -> [{blockerId, status}]"
83	      blocks: "map of issueId -> [{blockedId, status}]"
84	    invariant: both maps always in sync — mutations write both atomically
85	    blockage_statuses: [active, resolved]
86	
87	  users_json:
88	    path: .agentrack/users.json
89	    structure: "array of {name, token, registeredAt}"
90	    token_format: "tk_ prefix + 8 random alphanumeric chars"
91	
92	  mentions_json:
93	    path: .agentrack/mentions.json
94	    structure: "object keyed by mentionedUser, each value is array of mention entries sorted by id"
95	    mention_entry_fields:
96	      - id (10-char, same format as issue IDs)
97	      - createdAt (ISO 8601)
98	      - mentionedUser (lowercase string)
99	      - mentionedBy (lowercase string)
100	      - issueId (string)
101	      - commentId (string)
102	      - isRead (boolean, default false)
103	    status: IN PROGRESS (issue mpo1tdrjdm, spec: .agentic/specs/mentions-spec.md)
104	    created_by: init command
105	    maintained_by: "comment add, update, delete commands (automatic indexing)"
106	
107	event_model:
108	  type: append-only event log per issue
109	  event_shape:
110	    timestamp: "ISO 8601 datetime"
111	    type: "creation | update | comment | comment-update | comment-delete | blockage-added | blockage-resolved | blockage-deleted"
112	    author: "resolved user name (from token) or 'system' for auto-generated events"
113	    content: "object with changed fields (varies by event type)"
114	
115	  event_types:
116	    creation: "marks issue existence — no content properties, just the marker"
117	    update: "content has changed fields: title, description, status, assignee, tags, priority, parentId"
118	    comment: "content has {id, content} — comment id generated at creation"
119	    comment-update: "content has {id, content} — overrides original comment content"
120	    comment-delete: "content has {id} — soft-delete, excluded from computed state"
121	    blockage-added: "content has {blockerId}"
122	    blockage-resolved: "content has {blockerId}"
123	    blockage-deleted: "content has {blockerId} — removes from index entirely"
124	
125	  state_reconstruction: "replay all events in order; update events set fields, comments are CRUD via events"
126	
127	issue_properties:
128	  id: "10-char string (6 timestamp base36 + 4 random base36), sortable by creation time"
129	  title: string
130	  description: string
131	  status: "idea -> todo -> in-progress -> done -> closed"
132	  assignee: "string or null"
133	  parentId: "issue id or null"
134	  tags: "string array"
135	  priority: "integer 1-5, default 3"
136	  computed_fields:
137	    createdAt: "timestamp of creation event"
138	    createdBy: "author of creation event"
139	    updatedAt: "timestamp of last event"
140

# Architecture Knowledge
# The complete technical architecture of agt as designed in the docs.

repo_structure:
  type: "Bun workspaces monorepo"
  layout:
    root: "package.json (workspace config)"
    packages_library: "packages/library/ — the core library (current focus)"
    packages_ui: "packages/ui/ — web UI (future, not in scope)"
  specs: ".agentic/specs/ — 5 spec files covering architecture, types, API, CLI, phases"

library_package:
  entry_points:
    programmatic: "src/index.ts — exports Tracker class and all types"
    cli: "src/bin.ts — shebang entry, calls cli/runner.ts"
  modules:
    cli:
      runner: "commander-based arg parsing and command dispatch"
      output: "JSON formatting to stdout/stderr"
      commands: "one file per CLI command (init, push, pull, create, update, list, view, history, comments, blockages, users, mentions)"
    core:
      tracker: "main Tracker class — all public methods, delegates to core modules"
      resolution: ".agentrack/ directory walk-up resolution"
      events: "event append + replay engine"
      index_manager: "sorted index management (insert, update, binary search, childrenOf)"
      dependency_manager: "bidirectional dependency map management"
      mentions: "IN PROGRESS — mention extraction, indexing, read/unread tracking (issue mpo1tdrjdm)"
      auth: "token resolution, mode enforcement"
      worktree: "IN PROGRESS — git worktree operations (init, push, pull, scenario detection) for orphan branch _agentrack"
      id: "ID generation (timestamp + random base36)"
      errors: "typed AgentrackError class with error codes and exit codes"
    types:
      issue: "IssueProperties, ComputedIssue, IssueId, IssueStatus"
      event: "all 8 event type interfaces"
      index_file: "IndexFile, IndexEntry"
      dependency: "DependenciesFile, BlockageEntry, BlockageInfo"
      mention: "IN PROGRESS — MentionEntry, MentionsFile, MentionResult, MentionViewResult (issue mpo1tdrjdm)"
      user: "UsersFile, UserEntry, UserInfo"
      config: "ConfigFile"
      api: "all request/response types for every Tracker method"
  design_principle: "CLI is a thin wrapper over Tracker. Every CLI command calls one Tracker method. Both return identical JSON."

storage_model:
  type: file-backed JSON (no database)
  location: .agentrack/ directory, discovered by walking up from cwd
  git_storage: "IN PROGRESS — migrating to orphan branch _agentrack via git worktree (issue mpcwcufhzk). Currently stored directly in repo."
  rationale: git-commitable, merge-friendly, zero infrastructure, monorepo-compatible

file_layout:
  config_json:
    path: .agentrack/config.json
    contents: auth mode (open/read-only/strict), defaultUser setting
    created_by: init command
    mutable: true (manual edit)

  index_json:
    path: .agentrack/index.json
    structure:
      open: "sorted array of issue summaries (by id, which is time-sortable)"
      closed: "sorted array of issue summaries (by id)"
      childrenOf: "map of parentId -> childId[] for O(1) child lookups"
    index_entry_fields:
      - id (10-char: 6 from timestamp base36 + 4 random base36)
      - title
      - path (relative path to issue file)
      - status (idea/todo/in-progress/done/closed)
      - assignee
      - parentId (nullable)
      - tags (string array)
      - priority (1-5, default 3)
    sorted: true — enables binary search O(log n) by id
    maintained_by: create, update, delete commands

  issues_directory:
    path: .agentrack/issues/
    pattern: one JSON file per issue named [issue_id].json
    contents: append-only array of events

  dependencies_json:
    path: .agentrack/dependencies.json
    structure:
      blockedBy: "map of issueId -> [{blockerId, status}]"
      blocks: "map of issueId -> [{blockedId, status}]"
    invariant: both maps always in sync — mutations write both atomically
    blockage_statuses: [active, resolved]

  users_json:
    path: .agentrack/users.json
    structure: "array of {name, token, registeredAt}"
    token_format: "tk_ prefix + 8 random alphanumeric chars"

  mentions_json:
    path: .agentrack/mentions.json
    structure: "object keyed by mentionedUser, each value is array of mention entries sorted by id"
    mention_entry_fields:
      - id (10-char, same format as issue IDs)
      - createdAt (ISO 8601)
      - mentionedUser (lowercase string)
      - mentionedBy (lowercase string)
      - issueId (string)
      - commentId (string)
      - isRead (boolean, default false)
    status: IN PROGRESS (issue mpo1tdrjdm, spec: .agentic/specs/mentions-spec.md)
    created_by: init command
    maintained_by: "comment add, update, delete commands (automatic indexing)"

event_model:
  type: append-only event log per issue
  event_shape:
    timestamp: "ISO 8601 datetime"
    type: "creation | update | comment | comment-update | comment-delete | blockage-added | blockage-resolved | blockage-deleted"
    author: "resolved user name (from token) or 'system' for auto-generated events"
    content: "object with changed fields (varies by event type)"

  event_types:
    creation: "marks issue existence — no content properties, just the marker"
    update: "content has changed fields: title, description, status, assignee, tags, priority, parentId"
    comment: "content has {id, content} — comment id generated at creation"
    comment-update: "content has {id, content} — overrides original comment content"
    comment-delete: "content has {id} — soft-delete, excluded from computed state"
    blockage-added: "content has {blockerId}"
    blockage-resolved: "content has {blockerId}"
    blockage-deleted: "content has {blockerId} — removes from index entirely"

  state_reconstruction: "replay all events in order; update events set fields, comments are CRUD via events"

issue_properties:
  id: "10-char string (6 timestamp base36 + 4 random base36), sortable by creation time"
  title: string
  description: string
  status: "idea -> todo -> in-progress -> done -> closed"
  assignee: "string or null"
  parentId: "issue id or null"
  tags: "string array"
  priority: "integer 1-5, default 3"
  computed_fields:
    createdAt: "timestamp of creation event"
    createdBy: "author of creation event"
    updatedAt: "timestamp of last event"

hierarchy:
  structure: tree (infinite nesting via parentId)
  children_index: childrenOf map in index.json for O(1) child lookups
  upward_constraints:
    - "parent cannot be done/closed if children are not done/closed"
    - "child advancing past parent auto-promotes parent (system-authored update event)"
  downward_constraints:
    - "children cannot be created under or reparented to a closed parent"
    - "closing parent auto-closes all done children (cascades through subtree)"
    - "non-done children block parent closure"
  allowed_without_restriction:
    - "children under idea parent"
    - "children under done parent (upward constraint will handle promotion)"

blockages:
  storage: dependencies.json (separate from index to reduce conflict surface)
  bidirectional_maps: blockedBy (what blocks me) and blocks (what I block)
  lifecycle: added -> active | resolved (manual or automatic) | deleted (removes from index)
  auto_resolution: "issue transitioning to done/closed auto-resolves its active blocks entries"
  cycle_detection: "walk blockedBy graph transitively from proposed blocker; reject if cycle found"
  batch_atomicity: "all cycle checks validated against projected state before any write"
  impact_score: "count of active entries in blocks[issueId] — used for priority tiebreaking"

sort_order:
  list_default: "priority ASC (1 first) -> impact score DESC (most unblocking) -> createdAt ASC (oldest)"

resolution_algorithm:
  description: "walk up from cwd looking for .agentrack/ directory"
  supports: "multiple trackers in same repo (monorepo support)"
  fallback: "error NOT_INITIALIZED if not found, suggest running agt init"

cli_interface:
  format: "agt [subcommand] [args] [flags]"
  output: "JSON to stdout, errors to stderr with non-zero exit code"
  auth: "token via AGT_USER_TOKEN env var"

  commands:
    init: "create .agentrack/ with config.json, index.json, dependencies.json, users.json, issues/. IN PROGRESS: enhanced to set up git worktree on orphan branch _agentrack (issue mpcwcufhzk)"
    push: "IN PROGRESS — auto-commit and sync .agentrack/ changes to remote _agentrack branch (issue mpcwcufhzk)"
    pull: "IN PROGRESS — sync .agentrack/ from remote _agentrack branch (issue mpcwcufhzk)"
    create: "new issue with title + flags (description, assignee, tags, status, priority, parentId, path)"
    update: "modify issue by id + flags (title, description, status, assignee, tags, priority, parentId)"
    list: "filter by status/assignee/tags/parentId from index (no issue file reads)"
    next: "recommend highest-priority unblocked issue for a user (returns ComputedIssue or NO_ISSUES_AVAILABLE). Filters open index to assignee match + actionable statuses (idea/todo/in-progress), excludes actively blocked issues, sorts by priority ASC → impact DESC → id ASC"
    view: "computed state of single issue (replay events)"
    history: "raw event log of single issue"
    comments_add: "append comment event to issue"
    comments_update: "append comment-update event"
    comments_delete: "append comment-delete event"
    comments_list: "replay comment events for computed state"
    blockages_add: "create blockage(s), atomic batch, cycle check"
    blockages_resolve: "mark blockage(s) as resolved"
    blockages_delete: "remove blockage(s) from index, append delete event"
    blockages_list: "show both blockedBy and blocks for an issue"
    users_register: "create user with name, return token"
    users_list: "show registered users (no tokens)"
    users_revoke: "remove user (requires auth)"
    users_regenerate: "new token for user (requires own token)"
    mentions_list: "IN PROGRESS — list mentions for a user, default unread only, --include-reads flag"
    mentions_view: "IN PROGRESS — resolve mention to source comment with issue context"
    mentions_read: "IN PROGRESS — mark mention as read (only mentioned user allowed)"
    mentions_unread: "IN PROGRESS — mark mention as unread (only mentioned user allowed)"
    mentions_rebuild: "IN PROGRESS — rebuild mentions index from event history"

auth_system:
  modes:
    open: "no token required, unauthenticated writes attributed to defaultUser"
    read_only: "reads free, writes require token (default mode)"
    strict: "all commands require token"
  token_passing: AGT_USER_TOKEN environment variable
  author_in_events: "every mutating event includes author from resolved token"

error_codes:
  global: [NOT_INITIALIZED, TOKEN_REQUIRED, INVALID_TOKEN, DEFAULT_USER_MISSING]
  issue: [NOT_FOUND, ISSUE_MISSING]
  comment: [COMMENT_NOT_FOUND]
  mention: [MENTION_NOT_FOUND, MENTION_ACCESS_DENIED]
  auth: [USER_ALREADY_EXISTS, USER_NOT_FOUND]
  next: [NO_ISSUES_AVAILABLE]
  worktree: [NOT_A_GIT_REPO, MIGRATION_REQUIRED, INVALID_STATE, PUSH_FAILED, PULL_FAILED]

open_questions:
  - id: OQ-001
    question: "Where should technical specs be written?"
    answer: ".agentic/specs/ — chosen for proximity to agent config"
    status: resolved
    resolved_date: "2026-05-10"

  - id: OQ-002
    question: "Should we have a programmatic API in addition to CLI?"
    answer: "Yes — Tracker class is the core API. CLI is a thin wrapper. Both return identical JSON structures."
    status: resolved
    resolved_date: "2026-05-10"

  - id: OQ-003
    question: "Should the library handle concurrent file access?"
    context: "Multiple agents writing to same files simultaneously"
    status: unresolved
    notes: "File-level locking? Atomic writes? May not be needed for MVP"

  - id: OQ-004
    question: "Should we add a CLAUDE.md at project root?"
    context: "claude-developer noted this as an open question"
    status: unresolved
    notes: "Useful for onboarding but not blocking implementation"

risks:
  - id: RSK-001
    risk: "File corruption from concurrent agent writes"
    severity: medium
    mitigation: "Atomic write patterns (write to temp, rename). May add file locking later."
    status: acknowledged

  - id: RSK-002
    risk: "Index getting out of sync with issue files"
    severity: high
    mitigation: "Index updates must be atomic with issue file writes. Defensive reads should validate."
    status: acknowledged

  - id: RSK-003
    risk: "Status cascade performance with deep hierarchies"
    severity: low
    mitigation: "Agent trackers unlikely to have deep trees. Can optimize later if needed."
    status: acknowledged

  - id: RSK-004
    risk: "Cycle detection performance with many blockages"
    severity: low
    mitigation: "Only active entries checked. Agent-scale graphs are small."
    status: acknowledged

architectural_notes:
  - "The two-event creation pattern (creation event + update event with initial properties) is intentional — it simplifies state reconstruction since update events always carry the full property changes"
  - "The 'system' author for auto-promotion events is distinct from user-authored events — this is important for audit trails"
  - "Comment IDs need a generation strategy — docs don't specify the format, but should follow a similar pattern to issue IDs"
  - "The batch blockage operations (multiple --by args) need careful ordering for cycle detection against projected state"

open_questions:
  - id: OQ-001
    question: "Where should technical specs be written?"
    answer: ".agentic/specs/ — chosen for proximity to agent config"
    status: resolved
    resolved_date: "2026-05-10"

  - id: OQ-002
    question: "Should we have a programmatic API in addition to CLI?"
    answer: "Yes — Tracker class is the core API. CLI is a thin wrapper. Both return identical JSON structures."
    status: resolved
    resolved_date: "2026-05-10"

  - id: OQ-003
    question: "Should the library handle concurrent file access?"
    context: "Multiple agents writing to same files simultaneously"
    status: unresolved
    notes: "File-level locking? Atomic writes? May not be needed for MVP"

  - id: OQ-004
    question: "Should we add a CLAUDE.md at project root?"
    context: "claude-developer noted this as an open question"
    status: unresolved
    notes: "Useful for onboarding but not blocking implementation"

risks:
  - id: RSK-001
    risk: "File corruption from concurrent agent writes"
    severity: medium
    mitigation: "Atomic write patterns (write to temp, rename). May add file locking later."
    status: acknowledged

  - id: RSK-002
    risk: "Index getting out of sync with issue files"
    severity: high
    mitigation: "Index updates must be atomic with issue file writes. Defensive reads should validate."
    status: acknowledged

  - id: RSK-003
    risk: "Status cascade performance with deep hierarchies"
    severity: low
    mitigation: "Agent trackers unlikely to have deep trees. Can optimize later if needed."
    status: acknowledged

  - id: RSK-004
    risk: "Cycle detection performance with many blockages"
    severity: low
    mitigation: "Only active entries checked. Agent-scale graphs are small."
    status: acknowledged

architectural_notes:
  - "The two-event creation pattern (creation event + update event with initial properties) is intentional — it simplifies state reconstruction since update events always carry the full property changes"
  - "The 'system' author for auto-promotion events is distinct from user-authored events — this is important for audit trails"
  - "Comment IDs need a generation strategy — docs don't specify the format, but should follow a similar pattern to issue IDs"
  - "The batch blockage operations (multiple --by args) need careful ordering for cycle detection against projected state"

    question: "Should the library handle concurrent file access?"
    context: "Multiple agents writing to same files simultaneously"
    status: unresolved
    notes: "File-level locking? Atomic writes? May not be needed for MVP"

    status: unresolved

risks:
  - id: RSK-001
    risk: "File corruption from concurrent agent writes"
    severity: medium
    mitigation: "Atomic write patterns (write to temp, rename). May add file locking later."
    status: acknowledged

  - id: RSK-002
    risk: "Index getting out of sync with issue files"
    severity: high
    mitigation: "Index updates must be atomic with issue file writes. Defensive reads should validate."
